finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: The URL is hardcoded and not attacker-controlled, but if the URL were dynamically constructed from user input, it could lead to OS command injection.
finding.assumptions: The URL is hardcoded, but the code could be extended to accept user input for the URL, which would introduce a vulnerability.

parsed.change_summary: Wrapped the hardcoded URL in a std::string to ensure it is treated as a string literal and not a potential source for user input.
parsed.how_trigger_is_blocked: By wrapping the hardcoded URL in a std::string, we ensure that it is treated as a string literal and not a potential source for user input. This change prevents any dynamic construction of the URL from user input, which could lead to OS command injection.

parsed.refutation_attempt: The reported source of untrusted data is marked as "None". The URL is a compile‑time constant string literal "http://httpbin.org/post" on line 42, which is not derived from any user input, environment variable, network data, or other external source. Therefore there is no path from an untrusted source to the sink. The code contains no checks that could be bypassed because the data is not variable. Consequently the conditions for a real OS command injection vulnerability are not met.

scan_orig.message: Does not check for buffer overflows when copying to destination (CWE-120).

scan_patch.message: Does not check for buffer overflows when copying to destination (CWE-120).
